summary.text: Claude Sonnet, 30 Wikimedia Commons photos, single labeller (draft). Reliable: brand recall 90%, gap detection recall 89-100% (false alarms 5% with prompt v1 vs 19-29% with v0). Unreliable: exact shelf count 48-66% and facings 48-67% across repeat runs, price-tag count within ±2 63-73%. Treat counts as rough; see eval/RESULTS.md. Samples below show model output next to our labels.

model_output.category: wine (Alsace white and red, supermarket aisle)
model_output.notes: Angled shot with bottles cropped at the left edge and tapering away to the right, so no facing counts are reliable and none are given. The shelves look fully stocked, so no gaps are reported. The shelf count of 4 is approximate: the lower shelves are cut off at the bottom of the frame and the right-hand wall racks are a different fixture. Other bottles show partial labels (Pinot Noir, Riesling Vieilles Vignes, Sainte-Odile-style labels) but the producer names are not legible, so they are not listed as brands. Several price tags on the far right and top shelf are too small or angled to read, and the 6.09 and 5.53 tags are uncertain, so they are excluded from the count.

model_output.notes: Almost entirely Super Bock (Portuguese brand) with Kings Brau, Coral. Shelf count assumes the top shelf holding the large Mini cases is shelf 1 and the floor-level shelf with the 7,99€ promo is shelf 7. Facings are given only for products fully visible and countable; the Super Bock cans, boxes and bottle packs are partly cropped, overlapping or stacked, so they are omitted. Several price tags are partly covered by shelf-strip branding or too small to read with certainty. Shelf edges at the far right are cropped.

Fully stocked biscuit aisle photographed at an angle, with 5 shelf levels visible. Packs are stacked deeply and run off the right edge and into the left-side perspective, so no product can be counted fully and facings are omitted. No visibly empty shelf space. The far-left packs are too small or blurry to read, so no brands are listed there. The shelf-edge strips have no legible price tags. Pack text for Parle-G, Parle-G Gold, Marie, Milano, Golden Arcs, 20-20 and Krack Jack is readable. The top-left boxed assortments (gift tins and boxes) have no readable brand.

Other packs (Gigantic Buttons, Fudge Bites, Honeycomb, Speckled Eggs, Whips, Brazil Nuts, Choccy Eggs) are M&S own-label by their tags and pack text. The partial 'Colin the Caterpillar' pack is excluded because it is cut off and its pack text is not fully readable.
